entries.name: Tabu search
entries.definition: A memory-guided optimization framework that steers a search trajectory by making selected moves temporarily inadmissible from search history, allowing non-improving moves and, where specified, aspiration-based overrides.
entries.identity_notes: This record denotes the tabu-search framework through the original Part I formulation. It is not merely a list of visited nodes, Ant System’s per-tour feasibility list, or a global best-first frontier. Recency restrictions, aspiration and longer-term memory are configurable mechanisms; no single fixed tenure or exact prohibition rule defines all variants. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 301 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 37 and 37 lines respectively. All 13 unique hit contents were inspected: prior local-search candidate leads, Ant System’s feasibility-list distinction, and their saved reports/reviews. These were references to methods rather than existing candidate records. Six exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and seven native neighboring mechanisms were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Finite recency memory is not a proof of cycle freedom or eventual global optimality. Attribute-based restrictions can exclude useful unvisited moves, and aspiration overrides must be designed with their effect on cycling in mind. The Part II finiteness construction was not inspected or generalized here.

The simple pseudocode stops when no admissible move exists, while the subsequent prose describes releasing oldest restrictions to restore a move. These are distinct handling choices; the conceptual record does not silently present them as one fully specified executable algorithm.

Tabu tenure, attributes, aspiration thresholds, candidate lists, move connectivity, initialization and stopping affect the search. Choosing the best currently admissible move does not imply monotonic objective improvement or a globally optimal final solution.

The source also discusses probabilistic, strategic-oscillation and mixed-integer extensions. This record does not instantiate all variants or curate performance comparisons. Memory-based search need not be a reinforcement-learning task.

claims.statement: Maintain the current solution, the best solution found, a neighborhood of applicable moves and memory-based tabu conditions on moves or their attributes. In the simple cost-minimizing version, choose the best admissible candidate under the configured evaluator even when every admissible move worsens the current objective, move there, and update the best-so-far record only on improvement. Update tabu memory so recent reversals or selected attributes remain restricted for a declared tenure, then expire restrictions according to that rule. Attribute-based restrictions can exclude unvisited solutions that share an attribute with a recent move. In the aspiration extension, a move satisfying the declared aspiration criterion can be admissible despite tabu status. Candidate sampling or approximate evaluation may replace full-neighborhood minimization. Intermediate-term memory can intensify search around features of good solutions, while longer-term frequency information can diversify it toward underexplored features; these are framework components whose concrete rules must be specified.

entries.name: Guided local search
entries.definition: A local-search metaheuristic that repeatedly minimizes an objective augmented by feature penalties, increasing selected penalties at local minima to alter subsequent search while retaining solutions according to the original objective.
entries.identity_notes: GLS is the named feature-penalty procedure, not all tabu search, a hard prohibition of recently visited moves, or Fast Local Search (FLS), which is a separately combinable neighborhood-reduction technique. The authors relate GLS to the broader tabu-search framework; that relationship does not make every tabu algorithm and the specified GLS update identical. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 301 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 37 and 37 lines respectively. All 13 unique hit contents were inspected: prior local-search candidate leads, Ant System’s feasibility-list distinction, and their saved reports/reviews. These were references to methods rather than existing candidate records. Six exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and seven native neighboring mechanisms were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The source allows zero feature costs. If every utility is zero, the all-feature pseudocode makes absent features tie with present ones, whereas the prose says only local-minimum features are penalized. A concrete implementation must declare its zero-utility and eligible-feature convention; the record’s stated update is restricted to the positive-maximum case.

Curator qualification of Equation 1: equal penalties contribute lambda*p times the number of active features. They cancel from move-cost differences only when that feature count is unchanged. The source’s equal-penalty cancellation statement is therefore not universal for variable-cardinality feature sets.

Penalties are finite soft costs, not hard prohibitions. Their effect depends on lambda, objective scale, feature definition, move set and stopping. At lambda=0 the guidance vanishes; increasing penalties does not prove escape from every basin or convergence to a global optimum.

Local minima are relative to h and the chosen neighborhood, not necessarily g. A deterministic penalty update does not make an entire implementation deterministic if its initial solution or local-search routine is randomized. The manuscript’s TSP comparisons do not establish universal superiority, and no benchmark results are curated.

claims.statement: Choose binary indicators I_i(s) for nontrivial solution features, feature costs c_i, a local-search procedure and penalty scale lambda. In the inspected basic formulation the c_i are fixed and nonnegative, and penalties p_i start at zero. Repeatedly run local search from the current solution using h(s)=g(s)+lambda*sum_i p_i*I_i(s), where g is the original cost. At an h-local minimum s_star, compute u_i=I_i(s_star)*c_i/(1+p_i). In the nondegenerate case of positive maximum utility, increment p_i by one for every feature tied at that maximum, then resume local search from the same solution under the modified h. Penalization can repeat without an intervening move. Feature costs enter the utility ranking, not as extra multipliers in the displayed penalty sum. Retain and return the best solution found according to g, rather than choosing it by the changing augmented objective. FLS and other accelerations may be combined with the local-search subroutine but are not required by this baseline.

entries.name: Iterated local search
entries.definition: A metaheuristic that builds a single search trajectory among solutions returned by an embedded optimizer by perturbing the current accepted solution, rerunning that optimizer, and applying an acceptance criterion to the resulting candidate.
entries.identity_notes: The ILS framework includes the common local-minimum formulation but permits a more general, possibly stochastic or history-dependent embedded optimizer. Historical names such as iterated Lin–Kernighan and large-step Markov chains denote particular developments, not exact aliases of every ILS configuration. Single-chain search distinguishes the framework from population selection and distribution refitting; optional restarts and hybrids require their own declared choices. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 301 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 37 and 37 lines respectively. All 13 unique hit contents were inspected: prior local-search candidate leads, Ant System’s feasibility-list distinction, and their saved reports/reviews. These were references to methods rather than existing candidate records. Six exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and seven native neighboring mechanisms were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Perturbations that are too weak can return repeatedly to the same optimizer output; independent large perturbations remove the current solution’s influence from proposed starts and approach random-restart behavior. The full behavior still depends on the acceptance rule and the embedded optimizer.

A deterministic memoryless embedded routine supports the simplified basin-of-attraction picture. General stochastic or history-dependent routines need not define the same fixed partition; history-free transition descriptions cannot be assumed for every ILS variant.

Transitions between optimized solutions need not be reversible, and deterministic perturbations can produce short cycles. The framework alone is neither a target-invariant MCMC sampler nor a global-optimality or cycle-freedom guarantee.

Initialization, perturbation, local-search termination, acceptance, best-so-far bookkeeping and restart conventions must be declared for an executable instance. The source reports sensitivity to module interactions, including settings worse than random restart; no universal performance ranking or empirical result is curated.

claims.statement: Generate an initial solution and apply the embedded LocalSearch routine to obtain a current optimized solution. Repeat: perturb that current solution, apply LocalSearch to the perturbed intermediate point, then use an acceptance criterion comparing the current and candidate optimized solutions, potentially with search history, to choose the next current solution. Repeat until the declared termination condition. In the simplified deterministic memoryless setting, LocalSearch maps candidates into a reduced set of local optima, and perturbation followed by local search induces transitions among them. The general framework need not explicitly enumerate neighborhoods in that reduced space. Accepted variants include retaining only strict improvements, always accepting the newly optimized candidate, or temperature-dependent acceptance; improvement-only selection is not a universal requirement. Perturbation and acceptance may use history, and the embedded procedure can itself be stochastic or use memory.

reading_notes: Tabu Part I’s Section 2 chooses a best admissible move even when all worsen the objective, preserves a best-so-far solution and uses history-dependent restrictions. Its simple pseudocode stops on an empty admissible set; subsequent prose describes dropping oldest restrictions instead. The record preserves this implementation choice. The pseudocode was checked visually.

Tabu memory can store move attributes rather than whole states, excluding moves to unvisited states that share those attributes. Section 3’s aspiration conditions can override restrictions. Sections 8 and the opening of 9 discuss intermediate/long-term intensification/diversification and optional probabilistic choices. Full Part II theory and the detailed probabilistic algorithm were not inspected; no universal cycle-freedom claim is made.

GLS manuscript Eq.1, Eq.2 and Figure 1 were checked visually: h=g+lambda*sum(p_i*I_i), feature cost only in utility I_i*c_i/(1+p_i), and all positive-maximum utility ties are penalized. The best returned solution uses the original cost g. Calls start from the previous h-local minimum; multiple penalty cycles can occur without a move.

GLS allows nonnegative feature costs. All-zero utilities expose a difference between all-feature pseudocode and prose penalizing only present features. The record declares this numerical-boundary ambiguity instead of inventing a universal convention. The claimed cancellation of equal penalties requires constant active-feature count, as a direct Eq.1 calculation shows; a variable-cardinality counterexample reverses ordering.

The GLS source calls the penalty scheme deterministic and relates it to tabu search, but initialization/local search can be randomized and a named overlapping framework relation is not exact algorithm equivalence. FLS is an optional subroutine acceleration; only its role, not its full algorithm, was inspected. Conclusions explicitly caution against generalizing empirical comparisons.

ILS Chapter Sections 2.1–2.4 define a single chain in the output space of an embedded optimizer, with perturbation, reoptimization and acceptance. The local-minimum/deterministic-memoryless picture is a simplifying case, not a universal requirement. Pseudocode across PDF7–8 was visually inspected. Acceptance is on the optimized candidate, not the intermediate perturbation.

ILS Section 3.3 explicitly gives strict-improvement, always-accept and temperature-based criteria, and a restart variant. Transitions need not be reversible; deterministic perturbations can cycle. The source also describes parameter combinations worse than random restart. No numeric table/benchmark claim or stationary-distribution guarantee is curated.

Only declared pages were read. Other extracted or rendered pages—including ILS image19—are not claimed visually inspected. No source-provided implementation, optimizer benchmark or training job was executed.

native_neighbors.name: Simulated annealing
native_neighbors.definition: A stochastic optimization procedure that explores candidate configurations with temperature-controlled acceptance of cost-increasing moves and progressively cools that acceptance process to concentrate search on low-cost configurations.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This record denotes the temperature-scheduled optimization procedure exemplified by Kirkpatrick, Gelatt and Vecchi. Its basic symmetric-proposal Metropolis step is distinguished from fixed-temperature target sampling, generic annealing metaphors, training signal annealing and a proof that a particular finite schedule reaches a global minimum. The 1983 article is a primary formulation, not a claim of exclusive invention. claims.statement: Specify a sampling family f(x;v), initial parameter, sample size N, elite parameter rho and stopping rule. Optionally smooth the fitted parameter toward the old one via v_new=alpha*v_fit+(1−alpha)*v_old. claims.statement: In the inspected positive-distance traveling-salesman formulation, place m ants at starting cities and initialize pheromone trails. An ant at city i samples an unvisited city j with probability proportional to tau_ij^alpha * eta_ij^beta, where eta_ij=1/d_ij; normalize over the currently unvisited cities. Each ant stores its visited cities and returns to its start after visiting every city. After all tours are complete, the ant-cycle rule updates every trail as tau_ij_new=rho*tau_ij+sum_k delta_tau_ij_k, with delta_tau_ij_k=Q/L_k if ant k used that edge and zero otherwise. Here rho is retention, 1−rho is evaporation, and L_k is the completed tour length. Reset tour-specific visited lists and deposit accumulators for the next iteration while retaining the best tour found. Ant-density instead deposits a constant Q per traversed edge at each step; ant-quantity deposits Q/d_ij per step. Those variants do not use the ant-cycle complete-tour deposit.
